lean.statement:
∀ {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [inst_2 : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [inst_3 : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_4 : BorelSpace E] (W : E → ℝ),
  ContDiff ℝ 1 W →
    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x)) MeasureTheory.volume →
      have μ := MeasureTheory.volume.tilted fun x => -W x;
      ∀ (D : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 μ) →ₗ.[ℝ] ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp E 2 μ)),
        D.IsClosable →
          (∀ (a : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 μ)) (H : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp E 2 μ)),
              (a, H) ∈ D.graph ↔ ∃ φ, ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) φ ∧ HasCompactSupport φ ∧ ↑↑a =ᵐ[μ] φ ∧ ↑↑H =ᵐ[μ] gradient φ) →
            ∀ (ε : ℝ),
              0 < ε →
                ∀ (f : ↥(MeasureTheory.Lp ℝ 2 μ)),
                  ∃ u,
                    (∀ (v : ↥D.closure.domain),
                        ε * inner ℝ ↑u ↑v + inner ℝ (↑D.closure u) (↑D.closure v) = inner ℝ f ↑v) ∧
                      MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable (fun x => ↑↑↑u x) MeasureTheory.volume ∧
                        MeasureTheory.LocallyIntegrable (fun x => ↑↑(↑D.closure u) x) MeasureTheory.volume ∧
                          (∀ (ψ : E → ℝ),
                              ContDiff ℝ 1 ψ →
                                HasCompactSupport ψ →
                                  ∀ (v : E),
                                    MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ψ x * inner ℝ (↑↑(↑D.closure u) x) v)
                                        MeasureTheory.volume ∧
                                      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => ↑↑↑u x * (fderiv ℝ ψ x) v)
                                          MeasureTheory.volume ∧
                                        ∫ (x : E), ψ x * inner ℝ (↑↑(↑D.closure u) x) v =
                                          -∫ (x : E), ↑↑↑u x * (fderiv ℝ ψ x) v) ∧
                            ∀ (ψ : E → ℝ),
                              ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) ψ →
                                HasCompactSupport ψ →
                                  MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * (↑↑↑u x * ψ x))
                                      MeasureTheory.volume ∧
                                    MeasureTheory.Integrable
                                        (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * inner ℝ (↑↑(↑D.closure u) x) (gradient ψ x))
                                        MeasureTheory.volume ∧
                                      MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * (↑↑f x * ψ x))
                                          MeasureTheory.volume ∧
                                        (ε * ∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * (↑↑↑u x * ψ x)) +
                                            ∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * inner ℝ (↑↑(↑D.closure u) x) (gradient ψ x) =
                                          ∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * (↑↑f x * ψ x)
approved_definition_context: Lp functions are equivalence classes modulo almost-everywhere equality; displayed coercions choose measurable representatives.
A partial linear map has a linear domain and graph. IsClosable means its topological graph closure is single-valued; closure denotes that extension.
The tilted measure normalizes the exponential of its potential relative to the base measure.
LocallyIntegrable for volume means integrability on a neighborhood of each point. ContDiff order1 denotes genuine continuously Frechet differentiable; infinite order means smooth.

An inner product of Lp classes is the Hilbert L2 inner product; pointwise inner products of vectors are real inner products. A scalar function gradient is the inner-product representative of its Frechet derivative.
